title: The Best Used Car Apps
summary: Looking for the best used car app? Find out what the CarGurus app offers, including built-in deal ratings and Dealership Mode. Plus see how eight rivals, including Edmunds and CarMax, compare.
body_markdown:
We live and breathe mobile apps. We use them for messaging, banking, music, social media, gaming and just about anything else you can think of. An app is more of a commitment than a quick AI or web search because it requires a download, and anyone who taps ‘install’ is consciously engaging with a single organization’s products and services.


The same applies to used car apps, and there’s a plethora of options for shoppers who favor their interactivity, functionality and mobile-first designs. The best of the bunch do all of that and more.


## The Best Used Car Apps


- Our Recommended Best Used Car App
- What Makes a Car Buying App the Best?
- Best Used Car App breakdown
- FAQs


## Our Recommended Best Used Car App


CarGurus was the most downloaded car shopping app in the U.S. and Canada in 2025, according to data from digital intelligence specialist Sensor Tower. As with the wider **[CarGurus platform](https://www.cargurus.com/research/articles/best-used-car-websites)** , transparency is at its core; it’s the best app for used car deals because ratings are built into every listing, so users can immediately see if a car’s price is great, fair, or overpriced.


There is more to it than size and clarity, though. The CarGurus app features **[Dealership Mode](https://www.cargurus.com/about/free-tools)** , which is specifically designed for shoppers physically examining used cars on a dealership lot. Users can stroll along, phone in hand, and compare cars they see for sale. Dealership Mode indicates which car is the better deal, provides estimated costs, and serves up unbiased pros and cons and an AI-recommended best choice.


Prices often change if a car spends a while on a lot, and shoppers can sign up to real-time alerts for price drops and new matches for fresh listings, so they don’t miss a trick. All the above and more are why we think it’s the best app for buying a used car.


## What Makes a Car Buying App the “Best”?


- **Quality and Quality of Listings** : Buyers want easy access to an extensive inventory of top used cars.
- **Transparency and Trustworthiness** : Knowing cars are listed for a fair price and that the listing reflects the true condition are paramount.
- **Car Shopping Tools** : What’s an app without unique, mobile-only functions to distinguish it from a website?
- **Clear Filters** : Shoppers gravitate to simple, in-depth filters that allow them access to the cars they want.
- **Real-time alerts** : Distinct to apps, notifications keep buyers abreast of what’s happening with cars they’re interested in.


As with **[used car websites](https://www.cargurus.com/research/articles/best-used-car-websites)** , shoppers typically value transparency, quality, and quantity above all else. The most trusted used car buying apps need to get the basics right and place the listings at their core. Visible **[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/cargurus-shop-used-cars/id814517475)** and **[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cargurus.mobileApp&hl=en)** rating and reviews are key here.


From there, it’s about features and settings that complement its mobile format and distinguish it from the competition. Clear, simple filters are the gateways to the cars shoppers want, so they need to be straightforward to use on a phone or tablet screen and provide depth of search.


The sector has expanded from simple mobile listings to AI-assisted, concierge-style shopping tools, so the best-rated used car apps offer use tools and features. Data is a big one—the more information an app provides about used cars, the better, and help and advice with financing and trade-ins, can make an app the best for finding used car deals. Vehicle history reports, comparisons, expert review content, and anything that helps with the buying process are all worthwhile.


## Best Used Car Apps Breakdown


*App* *Key Strengths* *Key Limitations*


CarGurus Data-driven transparency and Dealership Mode for on-lot AI comparisons Not a direct-to-consumer retailer like CarMax or Carvana


CarMax No-haggle fixed pricing with a huge store network Shipping a vehicle not yet purchased may incur a fee


Edmunds Extensive review library and augmented reality garage tool Less emphasis on real-time deal ratings and real-time pricing


Carvana Fully online, end-to-end retail app Smaller inventory than aggregate marketplace apps


Autotrader Trusted name with a large inventory Comparatively basic deal ratings


Cars.com Huge dealer network, detailed filters, and instant sale offers Less data-driven pricing context than CarGurus


TrueCar Upfront pricing from certified dealers Not ideal for buyers who want to negotiate


Kelley Blue Book Industry-standard used car pricing specialist Focused on values rather than shopping


CoPilot New, AI-curated vehicle recommendations Less brand recognition than established apps


## CarGurus


**At a glance** : The most downloaded car shopping app in North America, pairing data-driven deal ratings with in-person tools such as Dealership Mode.


**Pros** :


- Deal ratings built into every listing
- Dealership Mode for on-lot, side-by-side AI comparisons
- Real-time price drop and new listing alerts
- Financing pre-qualification with no credit impact, plus instant trade-in offers


**Cons** :


- It’s a listings and research app, so there’s no direct communication with sellers


Data, deals, and transparency are central to the CarGurus app, which also happens to be the most downloaded car shopping app in North America. Every listing includes deal ratings, so buyers can see how a car’s price compares against its immediate competition, it has the biggest inventory of any online used car marketplace, arguably rendering it the best app for comparing car deals, and **[owners looking to sell](https://www.cargurus.com/sell-car)** can get offers from multiple dealers in under two minutes. All that applies just as much to the **[website](https://www.cargurus.com/research/articles/best-used-car-websites)** as to the app, but what the latter brings to the table is its unique Dealership Mode, which allows buyers to compare cars side-by-side on a lot. It shows the user how vehicles in front of them stack up on price—both the overall cost and the estimated monthly payment—so they can see which is the better deal and employs AI recommendations and impartial pros and cons to highlight the best choice. There’s a calculator, too, which lets shoppers add taxes, fees, and other extras to the total for a clear idea of exactly what they’ll pay, along with real-time notifications and pricing history for individual cars, so buyers can instantly find out if the price has dropped.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for transparency both before and during a dealership visit.


## CarMax


**At a glance** : A direct-to-consumer retailer app with fixed, no-haggle pricing and a nationwide store network.


**Pros** :


- Fixed pricing eliminates haggling
- Home delivery in select markets, plus vehicle transfers between stores nationwide
- Transferring a car between stores does not require you to buy the car
- No flood- or frame-damage inventory
- 10-day money-back guarantee on every vehicle


**Cons** :


- Inventory limited to CarMax-owned vehicles
- No stores in North or South Dakota
- Transferring a car not yet purchased may incur a fee


Simplicity is the name of the game at CarMax, as it specialises in fixed-priced sales. As with the website, the app’s emphasis is the lack of interaction with dealers/no haggling and facilitates deliveries of cars to the network of stores. The app’s core features revolve around that service, and its reservation, shipping, and appointment management functions are designed to tee up the whole process within a few taps. Inventory is clearly displayed with studio pictures and there’s also a finance and discounts section with perks for app customers. Vehicle history reports, pre-qualification, and finance payments are bundled in, too.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for outright simplicity and fixed-price sales.


## Edmunds


**At a glance** : A well-respected automotive industry name excelling at detailed content and with strong research tools.


**Pros** :


- Extensive library of expert reviews and vehicle comparisons
- Augmented reality garage dimension tool
- Loan and lease payment calculators


**Cons** :


- Less emphasis on real-time deal ratings than CarGurus


Edmunds is one of the best-known names in automotive editorial, and content is its real strength. The app allows users to tap into its vast library of expert vehicle reviews and user ratings, so it’s among the best in the business for research. It also has an extensive inventory of new and used cars, with filters aplenty, benchmarked against market prices so shoppers can see how a vehicle stacks up against the competition, along with its history. Loan and lease payment calculators tell buyers how much they can expect to shell out each month, and they can text dealers via the app to enquire about offers and discounts. The ‘Can It Fit?’ augmented reality feature is a real highlight, as users can scan their garage, parking space, or driveway to determine whether it can accommodate a potential purchase.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for research.


## Carvana


**At a glance** : A fully online, end-to-end retailer app covering financing, trade-in, and home delivery.


**Pros** :


- Do absolutely everything in the app
- Full online buying with available home delivery
- Interactive 360-degree car views


**Cons** :


- Smaller inventory than aggregate marketplace apps


As with CarMax, Carvana is a fully online retail operation, and its app is geared for the same self-contained approach. At around 45,000 cars, its inventory is far from the biggest on the market, but it’s big on the instantaneous—that includes personalised finance terms, digitally buying the car, and having it delivered to your home or to one of Carvana's car vending machines—all via the app. The 360-degree spinner tool is a neat function for shoppers who want to digitally poke around a car’s exterior and interior, and other features include delivery tracking, a complimentary Carfax report, and the ability to sell and trade-in your car.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for buyers who want to do the entire purchase without leaving one app.


## Autotrader


**At a glance** : One of the most established names in used car listings with tools to help shoppers unsure about their next car.


**Pros** :


- Large, well-known dealer inventory
- Multiple functions to help shoppers settle on a car
- Saved search and favorites


**Cons** :


- Deal ratings not as detailed as with some other apps


Buyers flock to Autotrader in their droves because it’s one of the best-known names in the business and has a whopper of an inventory. Autotrader doesn’t do deal ratings like CarGurus, but it breaks down pricing to illustrate elements such as list prices, delivery and handling fees and downpayments, and it’s particularly good for shoppers scratching their heads about what car to buy. There’s an AI search facility to help undecided shoppers whittle down their choices (CarGurus’ equivalent is the **[Ask Guru tool](https://www.cargurus.com/discover)** ), a function to search for cars solely by keyword, and those who can’t find what they’re looking for can input search criteria to receive updates when cars that fit the bill are added to the site. Other features include vehicle history reports, an estimated payments calculator, and price-drop alerts.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for shoppers undecided about their next car purchase.


## Cars.com


**At a glance** : Massive dealer network, detailed search filters, and instant offers for sellers.


**Pros** :


- Said to be the biggest inventory going
- Shoppers can search by minute detail
- Car value tracker and instant offers from dealers


**Cons** :


- Less data-driven pricing context than CarGurus


This app is a portal to what is claimed to be one of the biggest dealer inventories in the country, with up to two million cars listed. It also says it has 10 million dealership reviews and allows buyers to pick a top-rated showroom. Breadth aside, the vehicle search facility is among its strongest suits, as shoppers can search by very specific factors such as vehicle color and certain types of technology, such as Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. It’s arguably the best of the apps for anyone who wants to sell, because it includes a value tracker to show how your car’s market price stacks up at any given time, plus an instant offer function that pairs sellers with dealers willing to buy.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Sheer inventory and instant sale offers.


## TrueCar


**At a glance** : An app built around upfront, no-haggle pricing sourced directly from a certified dealer network.


**Pros** :


- Upfront pricing from certified dealers
- Simple, guided buying process
- Handy budget calculator


**Cons** :


- Not ideal for those keen to negotiate with dealers


Clarity and personalization are TrueCar’s things. It isn’t quite as focused on fixed pricing as, say, CarMax, but claims to offer users an individual price from a certified dealer, along with a breakdown of the MSRP and any incentives, so there’s a big emphasis on knowing everything upfront. The app covers both new and used cars, has a buy online function and a budget calculator to illustrate how much users can afford. It also includes condition report summaries and, as with CarGurus and Cars.com, there’s a trade-in function.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for a full breakdown of pricing upfront.


## Kelley Blue Book


**At a glance** : The gold standard in used car valuation data.


**Pros** :


- The go-to used car pricing specialist
- 100-year-old brand
- Granular valuation detail


**Cons** :


- More price guide than a buying and shopping portal


Kelley Blue Book is to used car data what Superman is to superheroes—the original and the one everyone knows. The brand has specialized in pricing since 1926 and quite rightly says its personnel “wrote the book” on car values. The app continues in that vein, with a no-fuss layout designed to show exactly what new and used cars are worth and a full breakdown of the figures and values, including MSRP, certified pre-owned, suggested retail, private party and trade-in values.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for arming shoppers to the teeth with data.


## CoPilot


**At a glance** : An AI-native, subscription-free shopping agent that searches local dealers and ranks results.


**Pros** :


- AI-curated, ranked vehicle recommendations
- Chat-based assistant for buying questions
- Dealers cannot pay for placement


**Cons** :


- New entrant with less brand recognition than established apps


A relatively new kid on the block and big on artificial intelligence, CoPilot’s hook is an AI agent that claims to do all the used car shopping legwork. It says it scans local dealers and analyzes millions of cars based on market trends and buyers’ preferences, producing personalized rankings of cars that fit the profile for the right price. It claims never to share shoppers’ information and to keep dealers at arm’s length—it says they can’t pay to influence results—so buyers can let the tech do the work until they’re ready to go ahead with a purchase.


**Why You Should Consider This App** : Best for kicking back and letting the tech do the searching.


## FAQs


- Is it safe to buy a used car through an app?
- Which car buying app has the best trade-in tool?
- Can you buy a car entirely through an app without visiting a dealership?
- Which used car app has the best deal ratings or pricing transparency?
- Do car buying apps charge fees to buyers?


**Is it safe to buy a used car through an app?**


As with buying anything from anywhere, it depends what you’re buying and from whom, but reputable apps from well-known marketplaces use verified dealer networks, buyer protection services, and, in some cases, money-back guarantees—all of which should be clear on the app itself well ahead of a checkout screen. Nonetheless, there is no substitute for a real-world test drive and an in-person inspection of a used car.


**Which car buying app has the best trade-in tool?**


You’d expect us to say it, but we wouldn’t recommend it if we didn’t consider it a top choice. CarGurus’ **[offers](https://www.cargurus.com/sell-car)** section can generate offers from multiple local dealers in less than two minutes and allows sellers to compare them side-by-side. It certainly isn’t the only option, though, as the likes of TrueCar and Cars.com, among others, also offer trade-in tools, so we’d recommend checking out a few.


**Can you buy a car entirely through an app without visiting a dealership?**


Yes, you absolutely can. Apps such as CarMax and Carvana specialize in fully online sales, to the point of having the car delivered to your home and/or—in Carvana’s case—to your nearest vending machine. Such services are very much a case of shopper’s choice; those who like that level of convenience will go for it, while others who prefer a more traditional buying experience will gravitate towards apps with conventional dealer listings.


**Which used car app has the best deal ratings or pricing transparency?**


This really is CarGurus’ forte, as both the website and the app were created with deal ratings and price transparency at their core. Great, fair, or overpriced deal ratings are included in every listing, and draw on our extensive price index and market data to give users the most objective overview of how a used car measures up in relation to its peers. Kelley Blue Book is also hard to beat from a used car valuation perspective, because it has specialized in pricing information for a century.


**Do car buying apps charge fees to buyers?**


Most consumer-facing car shopping apps are free to browse, and well-known apps such as CarGurus and Autotrader exist to put buyers in touch with sellers, so there is typically no charge for this service. Ancillary services, such as vehicle financing or any add-ons, usually come from the dealer or the lender, not from the app itself.
